notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

% The ladder network of the Dice paper's network verification benchmark
% (bench/dicebench.ml, gen_ladder), ported to ProbLog: $1 rungs over two
% wires, the program's argument. From (true, false), rung T + 1 (step T)
% gives (false, false) where the first wire is up and the rung breaks
% (flip 0.001), else (b, not b), b a flip 0.5, where either wire is up, and
% (false, false) where neither is. o1(T) and o2(T) are the wires after T
% rungs; the queries are the wires at the end, o1($1) and o2($1) as
% Roulette's ladder.rkt prints them.
rungs(1000000).
step(0) :- rungs(N), N > 0.
step(T1) :- step(T), rungs(N), T1 = T + 1, T1 < N.
0.001::breaks(T) :- step(T).
0.5::b(T) :- step(T).
o1(0).
o1(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, o1(T), \+breaks(T), b(T).
o1(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, \+o1(T), o2(T), b(T).
o2(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, o1(T), \+breaks(T), \+b(T).
o2(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, \+o1(T), o2(T), \+b(T).
query(o1(1000000)).
query(o2(1000000)).

# The ladder network of the Dice paper's network verification benchmark
# (Holtzen, Van den Broeck and Millstein, OOPSLA 2020; SHoltzen/dice
# bench/dicebench.ml, gen_ladder), ported to Alea.jl, whose own programs
# have no ladder: N rungs over two wires, N the program's argument
# (`alea_bench.jl --set N=...`). From (true, false), a rung gives
# (false, false) where the first wire is up and the rung breaks (flip
# 0.001), else (f, !f), f a flip 0.5, where either wire is up, and
# (false, false) where neither is; the value is the two wires after the
# last rung.
#
# The port follows the paper's text: each rung makes its flips when it
# runs, in the text's order (the break, then a flip 0.5 for each branch
# that sets the wires), and `@alea_ite` merges the branches as in the
# programs of Alea.jl's tour.
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const N = 5

function ladder(s1, s2)
    @alea_ite if s1
        @alea_ite if flip(0.001)
            (false, false)
        else
            f = flip(0.5)
            (f, !f)
        end
    else
        @alea_ite if s2
            g = flip(0.5)
            (g, !g)
        else
            (false, false)
        end
    end
end

function network()
    x = (true, false)
    for _ in 1:N
        x = ladder(x[1], x[2])
    end
    x
end

model() = network()

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; benchmark/modular/ladder.rkt of the Roulette artifact (Zenodo
;; 10.5281/zenodo.15253254), its last line changed to print the two
;; marginals o1(N) = P((#t #f)) and o2(N) = P((#f #t)) in full (print.rkt).
(require "print.rkt")

(define (main n)
  (let go ([n n])
    (cond
      [(zero? n) (list #t #f)]
      [else
       (define a (flip 0.001))
       (define b (flip 0.5))
       (match-define (list s1 s2)
         (go (sub1 n)))
       (cond
         [(and s1 a)
          (list #f #f)]
         [(or s1 s2)
          (list b (not b))]
         [else
          (list #f #f)])])))

(define SIZE (string->number (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define result (time (query (main SIZE))))
(statement
 (emit (format "o1(~a)" SIZE) (result (list #t #f)) (list #t #f))
 (emit (format "o2(~a)" SIZE) (result (list #f #t)) (list #f #t)))

% The ladder network of the Dice paper's network verification benchmark
% (bench/dicebench.ml, gen_ladder), ported to ProbLog: $1 rungs over two
% wires, the program's argument. From (true, false), rung T + 1 (step T)
% gives (false, false) where the first wire is up and the rung breaks
% (flip 0.001), else (b, not b), b a flip 0.5, where either wire is up, and
% (false, false) where neither is. o1(T) and o2(T) are the wires after T
% rungs; the queries are the wires at the end, o1($1) and o2($1) as
% Roulette's ladder.rkt prints them.
rungs(100).
step(0) :- rungs(N), N > 0.
step(T1) :- step(T), rungs(N), T1 = T + 1, T1 < N.
0.001::breaks(T) :- step(T).
0.5::b(T) :- step(T).
o1(0).
o1(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, o1(T), \+breaks(T), b(T).
o1(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, \+o1(T), o2(T), b(T).
o2(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, o1(T), \+breaks(T), \+b(T).
o2(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, \+o1(T), o2(T), \+b(T).
query(o1(100)).
query(o2(100)).
